amendments.body: The 6 conservation test fixtures in `conservation_regression.rs` are copied verbatim into `e2e_conservation.rs` (grazing_fixture, feeding_fixture, mortality_senescence_fixture, trim_fixture, water_change_fixture, plus helpers close_gas_exchange, disable_dic_shortcuts, dump_trace). Extract shared fixtures into a `test_fixtures` module (e.g. `crates/tank_core/tests/common/conservation_fixtures.rs`) or a `#[cfg(test)]` module in tank_core that both test files import. This prevents silent divergence when a fixture is updated in one file but not the other.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criteria require tests that are 'easy to extend when later shrimp, habitat, or chemistry work lands.' Maintaining identical 100+ line fixtures in two files will inevitably lead to divergence as future beads touch these scenarios. A single source of truth for fixtures makes extending them a one-edit operation.

amendments.body: Test 3 (`closed_system_mortality_senescence_conserves_n_and_c`) verifies trace evidence for plant senescence → detritus and algae senescence → detritus, but does not verify shrimp death → detritus via an explicit `assert_trace_delta` for `system:daily_shrimp` / `detritus.fine_g`. Add a trace assertion that shrimp death routes biomass to fine detritus, matching the doc comment's claim that 'shrimp death and plant senescence route biomass to detritus.'
amendments.rationale: The doc comment and bead description both highlight shrimp death → detritus as a primary conservation story. While the N/C conservation assertion implicitly covers this (if mass leaked, totals would drift), an explicit trace assertion gives a diagnostic signal about *which* pathway broke, consistent with the acceptance criterion that 'failures dump the full trace to a file for debugging.'

amendments.body: The `moderate_planted` source water profile has uncommitted local changes (alkalinity 0.9→0.58, bicarbonate 54.9→35.4) and tank_scenarios has an uncommitted photoperiod change (10h→12h) for medium_planted. These tuning changes should be committed before this bead is closed, since the shipped `test_planted_tank_day_night_cycle` relies on the medium_planted scenario parameters being stable. The first test run showed a marginal 0.096 pH swing (threshold 0.1), suggesting the committed parameters are right at the edge.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criterion that 'closed-loop grazing, feeding, and mortality/senescence cases stay within explicit N and C tolerances' implies all shipped tests pass reliably. If the medium_planted scenario parameters produce a pH swing that is marginal (0.096 vs 0.1 threshold), non-deterministic platform differences could cause flaky CI failures. The uncommitted changes appear to be tuning attempts that should be finalized.

payload.summary: The conservation diagnostics and regression tests are well-structured and meet most acceptance criteria. All 6 named test scenarios are implemented with clear doc comments, per-tick budget assertions at 1e-6 tolerance, trace dumping on failure, and an e2e runner with formatted pass/fail summary. The budget_helpers improvements (Element::label/unit, assert_per_tick_balanced) are clean. Data changes (stoichiometric DIC rates, exact nitrification alkalinity constant) are scientifically correct. Three issues found: (1) fixture duplication between conservation_regression.rs and e2e_conservation.rs creates maintainability risk; (2) test 3 lacks explicit trace assertion for shrimp death → detritus routing; (3) uncommitted local tuning changes for moderate_planted profile suggest the committed parameters produce marginal pH swing results. The pre-existing `nitrification_lowers_alkalinity_and_ph` failure in chemistry.rs is not caused by this work.
